text:
ashley: FYI I just got 3 high-severity support tickets about p99 latency spikes on the hosted generation API. Customers report tail latency jumping dramatically starting ~09:12 UTC.

raj: saw alerts too. p95 went from ~120ms to ~800ms and p99s are hitting ~2.4s on several routes. Graphs looked like a step up at 09:12.

mia: any recent deploys or config changes around that time?

deploy-bot: deploy completed by leo at 09:10 UTC -> rtx-serve v2.14.1 to prod-gpu.

leo: that deploy touched cache key normalization for prefix/KV cache (small fix) and bumped default cache size. I didn't expect regressions.

ashley: support tiket contents show repeated failures to warm KV cache; cache miss rate spiked from ~8% -> 62% for route /v1/chat/generate. Also seeing a lot of cache-eviction logs.

oncall: I'm seeing prefix cache thrash on node pool gpu-a. Eviction rate rate-per-min jumped. Looks like many small keys churn.

claire: could be the normalization change. If cache key hashing changed, existing entries won't be found -> cold misses and then eviction churn when clients send many varied prompts.

tom: pulled logs from one affected host. snippet:
```
[09:12:03] cache: key-miss tenant=acme prefix_hash=0x1a2b3c
[09:12:03] cache: insert tenant=acme prefix_hash=0x8f7e6d size=6KB
[09:12:03] cache: evict key=0x4c3b2a reason=overcapacity
[09:12:04] rpc: tail-latency=2345ms route=/v1/chat/generate model=redwood-13b
```

mia: that evict right after insert is classic thrash. We might be accidentally increasing the effective cardinality of keys (e.g., normalization bug that includes volatile metadata like request-id). Any signs of request-id leaking into cache keys?

raj: grep shows recent key build code concatenates tenant + prompt-prefix + maybe session-id in a new branch. I think session-id got included for some streaming path.

leo: Oops, I remember adding session-id to assist dedupe for streaming clients. Should've gated it. If session-id is high-cardinality we blow cache.

ashley: Mitigation ideas: 1) revert the normalization change if it's quick; 2) patch to strip session-id from cache key; 3) temporarily increase cache capacity on the affected pool to reduce churn; 4) route heavy customers to fallback model pool without prefix cache until fixed.

oncall: We can up cache size via k8s configmap tweak and rollout a small config restart on pool gpu-a. That is low risk and immediate.

claire: prepare a canary patch to remove session-id from key builder. Unit test should assert deterministic key on same prompt across sessions.

tom: support team needs a repro to confirm fix. Quick repro: call /v1/chat/generate in a tight loop with unique session-id headers and small prefixes, observe miss rate. I'll paste the curl loop: 
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 200); do 
  SID=$(uuidgen)
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Session: $SID" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' >/dev/null &
  sleep 0.05
done
```

raj: repro confirmed in staging. Miss rate jumps and evictions start immediately when session header varies per request. With static session header miss rate stays low.

leo: I'm opening a hotfix branch now to stop including session-id. Will push PR in ~10m.

deploy-bot: leo started a hotfix-runner -> branch fix/cache-key-strip-session.

ashley: while we wait for hotfix, let's increase cache size on gpu-a by 2x and lower eviction aggressiveness (temp). That should smooth tail latency while we patch. Oncall, can you coordinate the config change?

oncall: Doing it now. Patching ConfigMap cache.max_entries from 100k -> 200k and eviction_policy=LRU->LRU (keeping same) but bumping reservation. Rolling restart the pool nodes. ETA ~6m.

support-bot: Notifying impacted customers: "We're investigating increased tail latency; mitigation in progress; engineering patch incoming."

tom: after increasing cache size, p99 dropped from ~2.4s -> ~480ms within 90s. p95 back to ~150ms. Eviction logs still present but lower frequency.

mia: good sign. Once leo's PR lands, canary it to gpu-a then monitor cache hit rate and tail. If stable, roll to others.

leo: PR merged and deployed to canary subset at 09:37. Code change: removed session-id from cache key builder and added unit test. Patch snippet: 
```go
// key = tenant + ":" + prefixHash // do NOT append session-id
func buildCacheKey(tenant, prefix string) string {
  p := normalize(prefix)
  return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%x", tenant, sha1.Sum([]byte(p)))
}
```

raj: canary metrics: miss rate back to baseline ~10% within 3 minutes, p99 ~220ms on canary nodes. No further evictions spike.

claire: we should make this more robust: add a lint rule that prevents high-cardinality fields in cache key assemblies and add a metric for unique cache key cardinality by tenant.

ashley: agree. Action items:
- leo: roll hotfix to prod fully after 30m stable canary (done).
- raj: add unit/integration test for cache key normalization (in progress).
- mia: add dashboard tile for cache-cardinality and eviction-rate per-pool.
- tom: draft postmortem and customer note for escalations.
- oncall: revert temporary oversized cache once patch validated and eviction rate normal.

tom: quick customer-facing note draft: "We identified a bug in cache key construction that caused high-cardinality keys for some streaming clients. This increased cache misses and caused tail latency regressions. We've deployed a hotfix and are monitoring. We'll follow up with root cause and remediation details."

support-bot: Customers updated.

ashley: Great work team — saved the day. Let's keep monitoring p99 for next 24h and loop back for a short postmortem. :thumbsup:

leo: pushing final rollout now.

deploy-bot: rollout complete at 09:58 UTC.

claire: adding follow-ups to backlog: cache-key lint, cardinality metric, eviction-policy review, warmup synthetic load for canary nodes.

ashley: closing thread when postmortem is linked. Thanks everyone.
